answer: Each identity opens one river thread on the public river ledger, posts a 70-credit bond, and publishes inflow and outflow receipts. Auditors recompute conservation per thread: outflow must equal inflow minus the nadir reserve, a minimum flow no thread may draw below. The first thread pays 25; the kth from one operator pays 25+3(k-1), so the 1000th pays 3022 and 1,000 fake threads cost 1,523,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. A rented-thread ring fails because receipts are key-bound to one thread, and a reused receipt burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 25 once, then recovers its bond.
